# `⍃` — Before

`f⍃g Y` is `(f Y)g Y`: `f` prepares the left argument of `g`. Operators bind from the left, so `3⍃<⍃/` is `(3⍃<)⍃/`, which computes a mask and then filters.

```bpl
-⍃+ 5              ⍝ 0
3⍃<⍃#2 7 1 8       ⍝ 7 8
' '⍃≠⍃⊆"a bc  d"   ⍝ "a" "bc" "d"
```

`X f⍃g Y` is `(f X)g Y`.

```bpl
10 -⍃+ 3           ⍝ ¯7
```

`A⍃f` binds the left argument. The bound function takes one argument. A train binds the same way: `10- y` is `(10⍃-)y`.

```bpl
10⍃- 3             ⍝ 7
32+1.8⍃× 100       ⍝ 212
```

See [After](after.qmd), [Atop / Rank](rank.qmd) and [Over](over.qmd).
